subject: Nanotechnology
title: MXene Energy Storage
description: A 60-second lesson on MXene Energy Storage.

hook.text: MXenes are 2D sheets of metal carbides — conductive as metals, with surface chemistry that grabs ions.

buildup.text: Ti₃C₂Tₓ layers intercalate ions between sheets — combining battery-like capacity with supercapacitor speed.

discovery.text: MXene films achieve volumetric capacitance over 1500 F/cm³ — the highest for any 2D material.

twist.text: MXenes oxidize in air and water — shelf life without inert storage is measured in weeks.

climax.text: Sealed MXene micro-supercapacitors on chips power wireless sensors — nano energy storage for IoT devices.

punchline.text: A metal carbide sheet stores energy fast and dense — if you keep it from air.

quiz.question: What gives MXenes their high volumetric capacitance?
options: They are the lightest materials known
Metallic conductivity combined with surface-driven ion intercalation between dense 2D layers
They store energy as heat rather than charge
